messages.content: You are running inside SolidCraft, a parametric 3D CAD application, as the user's assistant. The open design is reachable through the `solidcraft-app` MCP server: use its tools (list_commands, batch, execute, inspect_design, measure, screenshot, set_parameter, undo) to read and change the design the user is looking at, and verify with measure or inspect_design. Prefer one `batch` over many small calls. Saving, opening or exporting files waits for the user's approval in the chat, and each message allows a limited number of changes. Don't use shell or file tools: work through the SolidCraft tools. Keep answers short.

On XZ, sketch an L with its outside corner at the origin, 50 mm wide, 40 mm tall, both legs 8 mm thick. Fully constrain it with four driving dimensions (width, height, both leg thicknesses), then extrude 30 mm.

function.description: The command catalog: id, label, toolbar tab/panel, shortcut, one-line parameter docs and whether the command is enabled right now. Ids are dotted and lower-case (solid.extrude, sketch.create, solid.fillet, sketch.inspect, timeline.rollback). Optional case-insensitive substring `filter` over id, label, tab and panel (not the parameter docs, so a command id finds that command rather than every command whose docs mention it).
function.name: list_commands

function.description: One command's parameter docs and, for commands with a typed contract (solid.box, solid.extrude and engine.describe so far), the JSON Schemas (2020-12) of its parameters (`input`) and of a successful result (`output`); null for the others.
function.name: describe_command

function.description: Run one command with JSON parameters, exactly as the toolbar, palette and scripts do. Never opens a dialog. Examples: sketch.create {plane: "XY"}; sketch.rectangle.two_point {p0: [0,0], p1: [40,30]}; sketch.circle.center {center: [20,15], radius: 5}; sketch.dimension {entities: [curve id], value: "width"}; sketch.finish {}; solid.extrude {distance: 20, operation: "cut"}; solid.fillet {edges: [[0,0,10]], radius: 3}; solid.box {length, width, height}. Lengths are mm; expressions may use parameters and units ("width / 2", "30 deg"). Returns the command's result; failures leave the design unchanged. Sketch commands that add geometry return created: {points, curves, constraints, dimensions}: the ids of what they added, stable and not reused after a delete (undo rewinds the counters with the design), usable right away in sketch.dimension, sketch.constraint.* and sketch.delete. Feature commands return the feature's id and name, every body (bodies) and the bodies the feature created, changed and removed (created_bodies, changed_bodies, removed_bodies).
function.name: execute

verbose.description: false: omit the full feature body list and sketch ids repeated outside `created`; keep created_bodies, changed_bodies and removed_bodies (default true)

function.description: Run commands in order, stopping at the first error. Each step is {command, params}. On an error the steps already run are undone (unless rollback: false), so the batch is all-or-nothing; the reply names the failing step (index from 0), its error, and every result before it. The usual way to build a part: sketch, draw, dimension, finish, extrude, fillet… in one call.
function.name: batch

profile.description: Like timings, and each step's `profile`: {boolean_ms, tessellate_ms, other_ms}, its time in kernel booleans, in tessellation and the rest (default false)

rollback.description: Undo completed steps when one fails (default true)

timings.description: Add `timings`: [{index, command, ms}] for every step run (the failing one included) and `total_ms` (default false)

verbose.description: false: a compact reply. Feature steps leave out the full body list (created_bodies, changed_bodies and removed_bodies stay), sketch steps the ids they repeat outside `created` (default true)

function.description: The whole design: user parameters (expression, value, errors), the timeline (features with type, suppressed, rolled back, error, warning, timing), bodies (volume, area, centre of mass, bounding box, face/edge/vertex counts), sketches (curves with ids and coordinates, points, constraints, profiles, degrees of freedom, solve status), assembly joints (what each origin is attached to: occurrence, the feature, face, edge or sketch curve its face names refer to, whether it resolves and why not; `execute` `joint.inspect {joint}` gives one), the active sketch, selection and undo depth.
function.name: inspect_design

joints.description: Joint definitions as joint.inspect gives them, when the design has joints (default true)

sketches.description: Full sketch contents (default true; false = summary only)

function.description: Volume (mm³), surface area (mm²), centre of mass, bounding box and face/edge/vertex counts of one body or all bodies, with totals. With `items` (one or two selections, as `execute` takes them: faces, edges, vertices, sketch curves, profiles): one item's length, area or position, a circle's, arc's or cylinder's `diameter` and `radius` (with `circumference`, or an arc's `arc_length` and `angle_deg`), a slot's `slot` sizes; two items' `min` and `max` distance and, where one is round, `center_distance` (centre to centre, or from its axis).
function.name: measure

items.description: One or two selections to measure instead of bodies, e.g. {"type": "face", "body": "Body1", "index": 3, "point": [x,y,z]}

function.description: The edges (index, midpoint, length, endpoints) and faces (index, name, area, centroid, plane normal, a `point` that lies on the face, and for a cylindrical face its `cylinder`: origin, axis, radius) of a body. Use an edge midpoint as the [x,y,z] point that picks the edge for fillet and chamfer; a face's point or its name picks the face for the face commands.
function.name: body_topology

function.description: Create or change a user parameter and re-evaluate the timeline. `value` is a number (mm) or an expression ("40 mm", "width * 2", "30 deg"); `expression` is the same thing under the name the parameters.change command uses. Give one of the two (both only when they agree). Returns the new value, the features recomputed (`recomputed`), the features whose earlier result for the same inputs was reused instead (`restored`, e.g. after setting a value back) and any features that now fail.
function.name: set_parameter

comment.description: Comment shown in the parameters table

expression.description: Same as `value` (the parameters.change name); give one of the two

unit.description: mm, deg or "" (unitless); default from the expression

value.description: Number or expression (or give it as `expression`)

function.description: Render the design and return it as a PNG image. Headless: a CPU render of the model, fitted to the view. Connected to the app: a screenshot of the window (source "window", the default) or a render of the model with the app's camera (source "model"). Both show an active section (inspect.section) with its cut face capped. `view` first turns the camera to a standard view or a saved named view (view.save), `camera` to              any camera (as view.apply). `grid: false` and `axes: false` leave the ground grid (on Z 0) and the origin's axes out of a model render. A body whose appearance is see-through (appearance.assign with an `opacity` below 1) is drawn see-through, so what is inside it shows: that is how to look at the body a cut would remove inside the material it meets.
function.name: screenshot

axes.description: false: leave the origin's three axes out of the render (see `grid`). Axes hidden with browser.visibility stay hidden

camera.description: Look from this camera instead: {target: [x,y,z], yaw, pitch, distance, fov?}                         (radians, mm; as view.save and view.apply)

grid.description: false: leave the ground grid out of the render. It lies on Z 0 and cuts through a part that straddles it. Model renders only: default true, or as the app shows it when connected; with `grid` or `axes` a connected screenshot is a model render, and source "window" is an error

height.description: Render height in pixels (model renders; default 600)

path.description: Also keep the PNG at this path

source.description: window = app screenshot, model = model render

view.description: Standard view (iso, home, front, back, top, bottom, left, right, fit) or the name of a saved named view                          (default: keep the current one; headless starts at iso)

width.description: Render width in pixels (model renders; default 960)

function.description: Export bodies to STEP (.step/.stp), 3MF (.3mf), binary STL (.stl), ASCII STL (format stla) or OBJ. The format comes from the extension unless given. URDF (.urdf) exports the whole assembly for robot simulators: a link per component placement with mass and inertia, joints from the assembly's joints, and STL meshes in metres written next to it (docs/urdf.md); RViz needs mesh_prefix such as package://robot/meshes/.
function.name: export

bodies.description: Body names (default: all; not with urdf)

effort.description: urdf: joint effort limit, N or N m (default 1000)

mesh_prefix.description: urdf: put before each mesh file name (default: none, so relative to the .urdf)

velocity.description: urdf: joint velocity limit, m/s or rad/s (default 10)

function.description: What the app is running or has queued right now, for every client: each request's connection and id, method, command id (a batch's step count), seconds since it arrived (running_s) and whether it still waits its turn (queued); `self` marks a request sent on the connection that asks. Answers at once, even while the app is busy, and never shows parameters. Ask it when a call timed out or the app seems slow, before sending a change again.
function.name: running

function.description: Undo the last change to the design.
function.name: undo

function.description: Start a new, empty design (unsaved changes to the current one are discarded).
function.name: new_design

function.description: Open a .solidcraft design file, a STEP file (.step/.stp: a new design whose bodies come from the file, as an Import base feature in a component named after the file; an assembly's parts become nested components) or a mesh (.3mf/.stl/.obj/.glb/.gltf: mesh bodies in such a component; a glTF file's nodes become nested components and its materials appearances); the result reports the component (id, component_name). Replaces the current design; insert into it instead with the file.insert_step (STEP) or file.insert_mesh (mesh) commands. A STEP file from a system that has Y up opens lying on its back: `up: "y"` turns its component a quarter turn about X (Y becomes Z). glTF is Y up, so it is turned by default (`up: "z"` keeps its axes). `names` picks what the bodies are named after when the solids' own names say nothing useful.
function.name: open

names.description: STEP, IGES, FreeCAD and Rhino. auto (default): keep meaningful solid names, replace placeholders with the nearest named product, else instance; solid: the solid's own name; product: the part's name; instance: the occurrence's name, else the product's

up.description: STEP and glTF only. z keeps the file's axes; y: the file has Y up, so its bodies are turned to stand Z up. Default: z for STEP, y for glTF

function.description: Save the design to `path` or its current file. The default is a design container; a .json path selects plain JSON. Set format to container or json to override the path.
function.name: save

format.description: Design encoding (default: JSON for .json, container otherwise)

path.description: Path to save to (default: the current file)
